mechanism: Swap the input-to-B identities of the equilateral and scalene triangles using two contour-color pairs. The source equilateral is paired with B scalene and source scalene with B equilateral. Targets treating these proposed part correspondences as fixed identities and rejecting a legal rotation of B; all original triangle shapes and the unmistakable square in C remain visible.
mathematical_solution: The input multiset contains two congruent disks, one thin rectangle, one small right triangle, one scalene triangle and one equilateral triangle. A, B, D and E each contain exactly that multiset under planar rigid motions (their original piece contours remain independently visible even when touching/overlapping in the drawing). C instead has a four-sided square where the small right triangle is required, while keeping the other five pieces. It cannot be formed from all six input pieces without cutting/replacing a piece. Thus C is the only impossible figure. The overlays trace existing edges exactly; they neither add a piece nor remove any original contour or fill.
human_gate: Twelve legal 1pt solid auxiliary overlays lie exactly on the four selected triangle contours, with exact context vertices. No new puzzle boundary is introduced. Source triangles, B triangles, C square, bar, all disks and option letters remain readable. The colored triangle pairs deliberately differ in side structure, which remains a visible way to reject the false correspondence.
